title: How the 1931 Hines band differed from the first
summary: Hines wanted a bigger band; Ed Fox knew nothing about music.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: Well, you were with Dave Peyton when Earl heard you and offered you the job with his band.
Yeah, offered me the job with the band.
And you were playing with the Regal Theater there?
Right.
So you went with Earl in '31?
Right.
Well, I was doing a little research, and his first band had Hayes Alvis --
Right.
Played all tuba on the recordings.
Oh, yeah.

On the recordings. And had two trumpets, one trombone, three saxes and four rhythm. And then in '31, just judging by the personnel on the recordings, you had -- you'd added a trumpet, added a trombone. So it's a bigger band.
And you have the enlarged band.
And the only hold-overs from the first band were Billy Franklin and Cecil Irwin.
That's right.
So evidently Earl, or somebody, wanted to change the band.
Yeah.
Do you know the reason for that?
No, I don't.
There's a great difference, musical difference between those two bands.
That's right.

You're playing string bass, which makes a great difference in the rhythm section. It would certainly be interesting to know what caused that change, because I think it was a significant change, musically, for Earl. And I just wondered whether it was Earl, or Ed Fox, or --
No, it was Earl. Wasn't Ed Fox, because he didn't know nothing about music.
